title: Shopify Fulfillment and NetSuite Integration
summary:
The meeting focused on improving Shopify, OMS, Rails, and NetSuite synchronization, with emphasis on partial payments, rejected orders, fulfillment mismatches, inventory accuracy, and integration scalability. Partial-payment handling remained unresolved pending guidance from the Rails team, while rejected-order synchronization options included a POS UI extension and an order metafield triggering an order-updated event.

Fulfillment discrepancies included changed locations, incomplete routed-item fulfillment, strict ship-group and facility matching, and store fulfillments not being marked or transmitted to NetSuite. Partial shipments are operationally common but unsupported by the Rails application. The team considered using Shopify fulfillment as the operational source of truth and updating OMS order items, but no implementation direction was finalized. Quantifying cases where Shopify shows fulfillment absent from the OMS was identified as important because unmarked store fulfillments can block NetSuite feeds and distort inventory across systems.

Location mapping discussions covered assigning a single Shopify warehouse location directly to its corresponding facility, propagating inventory changes across open channels, and updating physical locations in inventory channels. Testing limitations in Rails UAT prompted consideration of multiple Shopify stores or an equivalent sandbox. US cutover procedures were expected to apply broadly, although country-specific order mappings and shipping methods require validation.

The team reviewed warehouse-and-store reporting buckets and a Shopify fulfillment-history report intended to reduce downstream risk. Several pull requests remained pending, including functionality exposing fulfillment synchronization counts for pending, queued, and completed orders.

NetSuite integration work focused on throttling affecting simple operations and bulk workflows. The team questioned whether Return Sync represented the primary NetSuite code path and noted that other services still needed identification. A conference room participant presented Moki AI, Moki GQL, and Moki SSO, which support GraphQL, SSO, MCP-based Moki API access, chat interaction, and production debugging; the Moki AI implementation remained in a reviewable pull request.
action_items: Meeting participant will obtain the Rails team’s answer on how to handle partial-payment orders that do not sync with NetSuite
Meeting participant will determine how many Shopify-completed fulfillments are missing from the OMS
Meeting participant will evaluate the inventory impact of unmarked store fulfillments that are not reaching NetSuite
Meeting participant will investigate the location mapping configured in NetSuite
Meeting participant will set up a multi-store Shopify or comparable sandbox configuration for inventory-event testing
Meeting participant will review the single-location fulfillment case and determine whether routing should be applied
Conference room participant will confirm any additional services or NetSuite code paths beyond the primary Return Sync implementation.
Conference room participant will prioritize deployment of the Moki AI component.
Meeting participant will review the Moki AI pull request before it is merged.
Meeting participant will consult Deepak regarding use of the Moki SSO component.
topics: The partial-payment order synchronization issue with NetSuite remains unresolved pending input from the Rails team
Rejected orders may require a POS UI extension and an order metafield that triggers synchronization through an order-updated event
Shopify fulfillment mismatches are caused by changed locations, incomplete routed fulfillment, and strict OMS matching rules
Partial shipments are a common operational scenario but are not currently implemented in Rails
The team will first determine how many Shopify-completed fulfillments are missing from the OMS
Missing fulfillment updates are directly affecting NetSuite inventory synchronization
The team did not reach an immediate solution for reconciling order states across Shopify, the OMS, and NetSuite
Inventory changes need to be propagated across all relevant channels
A multi-store Shopify or sandbox setup was proposed because the complete inventory flow cannot be tested in Rails UAT
The proposed single-warehouse design maps Shopify’s location directly to the corresponding facility.
Fulfillment reporting will show warehouse and store configurations across several defined buckets.
Country rollout planning must account for country-specific order mappings and differing shipping methods.
The fulfillment status page will expose pending, queued, and completed synchronization counts to clients.
The team intends to improve NetSuite bulk operations, especially where throttling creates architectural problems.
Moki AI, Moki GQL, and Moki SSO were presented as deployable components for API access, chat interaction, and production debugging.
